singles/stewart-cadets/.title: Stewart Cadets
singles/stewart-cadets/.text:
[Dad calls each verse line. The boys echo it back.]

Dad: Stewart boys, fall in!

This is how we’ll handle you,
I won’t live inside a zoo!
Time to get this whole house clean,
March and scrub like a Marine!

I don’t know but I’ve been told,
Dust bunnies are getting bold!
Grab the broom and sweep the floor,
Get the crumbs behind the door!
Sweep beneath each kitchen chair,
Bet you’ll find some crackers there!
Get the corners by the wall,
Grab the dustpan, dump it all!

Socks and shirts go in the bin,
If you miss, then try again!
Fold your shirts and match each pair,
Put clean clothes away with care!

Scrape your plate and grab your cup,
Take them both when you get up!
Wash the front and wash the back,
Set them in the drying rack!

Dad: Sound off!
Boys: One, two!
Dad: Sound off!
Boys: Three, four!

I don’t know but I’ve been told,
“Just a minute” gets real old!
When Mom calls, I pause my game,
First time that she says my name!

Ask before you take it out,
Wait for yes so there’s no doubt!
If they tell you no today,
Hands off, boys, and walk away!
If they lend their stuff to you,
Bring it back when you are through!

I don’t know but I’ve been told,
Truth is worth much more than gold!
Don’t give Dad an “I don’t know.”
If you did it, tell him so!

Skip your chores and here’s the drill,
Five push-ups, then scrub that spill!
If you man up, do it right,
No more drills for you tonight!

Dad: Who did it?
Boys: I did, sir!
Dad: Who cleans it?
Boys: I do, sir!
Dad: What’s better than gold?
Boys: Honesty is better than gold!

Dad: Sound off!
Boys: One, two!
Dad: Sound off!
Boys: Three, four!
All: One, two, three, four! One, two! Three, four!

singles/the-stewart-zoo/.title: THE STEWART ZOO
singles/the-stewart-zoo/.text:
[Intro]
[Animal noises: a puppy yip, a raptor screech, a bunny thump, a platypus growl, then drums kick in]
[Spoken, kid voice]
Welcome to the zoo!

[Verse 1]
Samuel has a platypus, the strangest pet in town,
A bill just like a duck and a beaver tail that flaps around.
He lays eggs, but he's a mammal, now isn't that absurd?
He's the weirdest, wonderfulest critter ever heard!

[Verse 2]
John has a puppy dog with ears that flop and flap,
He chews up every shoe and he curls up on your lap.
He wags his tail so hard that it knocks the lamp right down,
He's the goodest, bestest puppy in the whole wide town!

[Chorus]
Four boys, four pets, what a crazy zoo!
Squeak and squawk and growl and yip, and a roar or two!
Four boys, four pets, and a house that's full of noise,
God made them all, and He made those boys!

[Verse 3]
Stephen has a raptor, feathers head to toe,
Turkey-sized and speedy, watch him go, go, go!
He tiptoes through the kitchen, “SKREE!” he wants a snack,
Mom says, “Not the pancakes!” and he gives them right back.

[Verse 4]
Daniel has a little bunny, Fu Fu is his name,
Twitchy nose and floppy ears, and he thumps when he's tame.
There's a rhyme about a Fu Fu who's a rascal, so they say,
But this Fu Fu's gentle, and he hops the nice way!

[Chorus]
Four boys, four pets, what a crazy zoo!
Squeak and squawk and growl and yip, and a roar or two!
Four boys, four pets, and a house that's full of noise,
God made them all, and He made those boys!

[Bridge]
[Drums drop out, handclaps only]
[Spoken, slow and big]
“Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord!”
[Platypus growl]
[Puppy: yip yip!]
[Raptor: SKREE!]
[Bunny: thump thump!]
“A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast.”
That means be kind to every creature!
[Drums crash back in]
Even the raptor!

[Verse 5]
Now the puppy chases the raptor, and the raptor chases a sock,
Fu Fu thumps on the couch while the platypus watches the clock.
Mom walks in the room and says, “Who let the zoo inside?”
Four boys point at each other: “It was him! I just got here!”

[Final Chorus]
Four boys, four pets, what a crazy zoo!
Squeak and squawk and growl and yip, and a roar or two!
Four boys, four pets

singles/all-aboardwith-daniel/.title: All AboardWith Daniel
singles/all-aboardwith-daniel/.text:
[Intro]
[Train whistle, chugging drums, handclaps]
[Spoken, kid voice]
All aboard!

[Verse 1]
Chugga chugga, chugga chugga, down the track we go,
A little engine rolling through the valley, nice and slow.
Puffing up the hillside, steam up in the air,
Toot toot! He's got a job to do, and he's glad to be there!

[Chorus]
All aboard, all aboard,
Jesus is the engineer!
He knows every mile of the track,
And He'll bring us safely there!
Chugga chugga, toot toot,
Stay right on the line,
When you follow the One who made the road,
You're gonna be just fine!

[Verse 2]
The engine reached a bridge that looked too high to cross,
He puffed and said, "I'm just too small," and he nearly stopped.
But the engineer said, "Steady now, I'm right here with you,
I built this bridge, and I'll take you through!"

[Chorus]
All aboard, all aboard,
Jesus is the engineer!
He knows every mile of the track,
And He'll bring us safely there!
Chugga chugga, toot toot,
Stay right on the line,
When you follow the One who made the road,
You're gonna be just fine!

[Verse 3]
Two train cars were squabbling on the siding one day,
"I'm bigger!" "I'm faster!" "Get out of my way!"
But the little engine rolled in with a smile,
He said, "Let's pull together, it's a long, long mile!"

[Bridge]
[Drums drop out, handclaps only]
[Spoken, slow]
"Blessed are the peacemakers,
For

singles/no-more-stinky-elephants/.title: No More Stinky Elephants
singles/no-more-stinky-elephants/.text:
Verse 1
There was an elephant, big and round,
The stinkiest one in the whole playground!
He wiggled his ears, he wiggled his toes…
Everybody shouted, “Hold your nose!”

Chorus
🎶 No more stinky elephants!
No more stinky elephants!
Take a bath and scrub, scrub, scrub!
Bubble, bubble, rub, rub, rub!
No more stinky elephants!
Hooray! Hooray! Hooray! 🎶

Verse 2
He splashed in a tub with lots of foam,
Rubber ducks came floating home.
He washed his trunk from tip to tail…
Now he smells like lemon ale! (Or sing “lemon pie” if you prefer.)

Chorus
🎶 No more stinky elephants!
No more stinky elephants!
Take a bath and scrub, scrub, scrub!
Bubble, bubble, rub, rub, rub!
No more stinky elephants!
Hooray! Hooray! Hooray! 🎶

Ending
If your elephant starts to stink,
Don’t you worry—don’t you blink!
Grab some soap and sing along…
Then everybody ends with:

🎶 NO MORE STINKY ELEPHANTS! 🐘✨

singles/god-made-the-dinosaurs/.title: God Made the Dinosaurs
singles/god-made-the-dinosaurs/.text:
[Intro]
[Big stomping drums, a loud ROAR sound effect, handclaps]
[Spoken, kid voice]
Ready? Stomp with me!

[Verse 1]
Tyrannosaurus rex was the king of the land,
Big old teeth and a teeny little hand.
He couldn't clap, he couldn't tie a shoe,
But God made him special, and He made you too!

[Chorus]
Stomp, stomp, stomp, stomp, ROAR!
God made the dinosaurs!
Big ones, small ones, spiky ones, tall ones,
God made the dinosaurs!
[Kids shout: ROAR!]

[Verse 2]
Triceratops had three horns on his face,
He stood up tall and held his place.
When a bully came around, he didn't run or hide,
He stood up for his friends with his dino pride!

[Chorus]
Stomp, stomp, stomp, stomp, ROAR!
God made the dinosaurs!
Big ones, small ones, spiky ones, tall ones,
God made the dinosaurs!
[Kids shout: ROAR!]

[Verse 3]
Brachiosaurus had a neck so long,
He munched the treetop leaves all day long.
He looked way up, up, up so high,
And said, "Thank You, Lord, for the big blue sky!"

[Verse 4]
Stegosaurus had plates down his back,
A spiky tail and a stomp-stomp track.
He wasn't like the others, he was one of a kind,
And that's how God designed him, with His wonderful mind!

[Bridge]
[Drums drop out, handclaps only]
[Spoken, slow and big]
"And God made the beast of the earth after his kind,
And God saw that it was good!"
"I am fearfully and wonderfully made!"
[Drums crash back in]
That means you!

[Verse 5]
Now Stephen draws a T-Rex with a great big grin,
Dinosaurs everywhere, and he's just getting started!
He knows the God who made them is the God who made him,
And He loves every roar and every stomp!

[Final Chorus]
Stomp, stomp, stomp, stomp, ROAR!
God made the dinosaurs!
Big ones, small ones, spiky ones, tall ones,
God made the dinosaurs!
And God made YOU!
[Kids shout: ROAR!]

[Outro]
[Big stomp, then a tiny squeaky roar]
[Spoken, kid voice]
Okay, that last one was me.

[End]

singles/are-you-still-thankful/.title: Are You Still Thankful
singles/are-you-still-thankful/.text:
[Verse 1 — Soft, Searching]
There was a shoreline.
There was a grave.
There were the people
God helped sustain.

Then came the harvest,
Corn, fowl, and deer.
Neighbors sat with them.
Thanks mingled with tears.

[Pre-Chorus]
They knew the hunger.
They knew the cost.
Even in plenty,
They knew what they’d lost.

[Chorus]
Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.
There are no presents,
Just thankfulness.

Bread on the table,
One day to live.
Still we depend on
The God who gives.

[Verse 2 — Slowly Building]
There was a nation,
Newly made free.
Washington called us
To bow gratefully.

Then came division,
Brothers at war.
Lincoln called wounded
Hearts to the Lord.

[Pre-Chorus]
Thanks for His mercy,
Prayer for our land.
Even in sorrow,
We needed His hand.

[Chorus]
Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.
There are no presents,
Just thankfulness.

Bread on the table,
One day to live.
Still we depend on
The God who gives.

[Verse 3 — Warm, Bittersweet]
Nineteen-fifty.
Chairs on the floor.
Grandma is coming;
One place for more.

Bread from the oven,
Hands worn with care.
Dad bows his head now.
We hear his prayer.

[Pre-Chorus]
Thanks for the wages,
Thanks for the rain,
Thanks for the mercy
That brought us again.

[Verse 4 — Growing Urgency]
Now there is plenty,
More than we need.
Phones at the table,
No time to speak.

Christmas is calling.
Sales fill the screen.
We’re making our wishes.
What does thanks mean?

[Bridge — Exposed Voice]
Why did we gather?
What was this for?
When did our blessings
Leave us wanting more?

Lord, I’ve been asking.
Lord, I’ve forgot
How much You’ve given,
How much it cost.

[Final Chorus — Full, Aching]
Are we still thankful?
Lord, help us say yes.
More than a dinner,
More than a guest.

You give the harvest.
You give us breath.
Still we depend on
Your faithfulness.

[Outro — Quiet]
Before it is Christmas,
Let us stay here.
Thank You for mercy
Through all these years.

Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.

[Let the final piano chord fade]

singles/the-other-guy/.title: The Other Guy
singles/the-other-guy/.text:
[Spoken Intro: low male voice, solo piano]
You're the man you swore you'd never be,
And pride has hurt your family.

[Pause]
The drink's gone warm, you turn your ring,
And think of every broken thing.

Or on the couch, the TV black,
Her coat still hangs. You want her back.
A drawing on the fridge, you standing tall.
Your sons don't know the truth at all.

[Pause, spoken freely]
You remember the boy you were,
And the man you promised to become.

You didn't.

You can't see past the man you are.

[Piano drops to one low note]
But wait.

[Verse 1: minor key, sparse piano and cello]
There was a man who watched them die,
Sure that he served the Lord.
And another man stood tall at the top,
"I built it all," he roared.

[Low, almost spoken]
Pride buries the good.

[Verse 2]
There was a man who lied to live,
And his son would do the same.
And another man disowned his friend,
And could not bear the shame.

[Low, almost spoken]
Lies leave us alone.

[Verse 3]
There was a man who took a life,
And ran away to hide.
And another man took from his own,
And counted coins while they cried.

[Low, almost spoken]
Stains don't wash out.

[Verse 4]
There was a man no one could beat,
Who kept on falling the same old way.
And another man won the biggest fight,
Then ran, and begged to die that day.

[Low, almost spoken]
Despair says, "You're done."

[Chorus: stripped back, sorrowful]
We always thought He'd choose some other guy,
Someone strong enough to never ask Him why.
We're the men we swore we'd never be,
How could God use men like you and me?

[Spoken Bridge: piano only, almost a whisper]
"Man looketh on the outward appearance,
But the Lord looketh on the heart."

[Pause]

Then Someone called their names.

[Verse 5: key lifts, drums enter, strings begin to rise]
That man who watched the innocent die
Wrote of grace that set men free.
And that man at the top who said, "I built it all,"
Looked up, and learned to see.

Grace lifts the proud.

[Verse 6]
That man who lied to save his life
Learned to trust what God had vowed.
And that man who disowned his friend
Heard, "Feed My sheep," and bowed.

Truth makes honest men of liars.

[Verse 7]
That man who took a life
Came back, and led them through.
And that man who took from his own
Left his table, and wrote what's true.

Mercy washes what we can't.

[Verse 8]
That man no one could beat
Gave his last strength in one prayer.
And that man who hid and wished it over
Found God still waiting there.

Hope says, "You're not done."

[Chorus: full band, strong male vocal]
There was no other guy,
Thieves and liars, blood on their hands.
They were never the hero,
But the Hero made them heroes.

[Spoken Reveal: slow and deliberate, soft piano, one name per drum hit, pause between names]
Paul.
Babylon's king.
Abraham.
Peter.
Moses.
Matthew.
Samson.
Elijah.

[Drums stop]
Men who fell.
Men who ran.
And God still called their names.

[Pause, quiet]
"And such were some of you:
But ye are washed."

[Final Verse: quiet choir enters, gradually building]
And somewhere tonight a man's in the dirt,
With a secret he's carried for years.
The screen in the dark, the bottle he hides,
The anger, the shame, the tears.

The job he lost, the words he said,
The lie he's afraid to undo.
The voice that says, "You're done, you're through."

[Brief silence]
Get up. Someone's calling you.

[Final Chorus: full band and choir, triumphant key lift]
There is no other guy,
It was never the strength of the man.
We're not who we swore we'd be,
But He's the God who makes men new.

The true Hero shining through
Every broken life surrendered.
We've got nothing left to prove.
Here we are, Lord. Make us new.

[Spoken: band softens, sustained choir]
"My grace is sufficient for thee:
For my strength is made perfect in weakness."

[Outro: piano alone, very quiet]
"Wait on the Lord: be of good courage,
And he shall strengthen thine heart."

[Long pause]
But wait.

[End]

singles/before-we-hang-the-lights/.title: Before We Hang The Lights
singles/before-we-hang-the-lights/.text:
BEFORE WE HANG THE LIGHTS

[Intro: gentle piano and fingerpicked acoustic guitar]

[Verse 1: intimate male vocal]
There’s a box of lights beside the stairs,
The boys are pulling out their chairs.
Dawn brings the last dish through the door,
We make some room and pass one more.
Someone asks, “Can we hang these tonight?”
I look around in the soft white light.
“We will, but first, before we do,
Let’s name the things God brought us through.”

[Chorus: quiet, warm, prayerful]
Before we hang the lights this year,
Let’s thank the One who brought us here.
Let the dishes wait, let the room grow still,
There’s a place in us that only praise can fill.
We name the times You brought us through—
There’s a story in each “thank You.”
Let our children hear those stories clear,
Before we hang the lights this year.

[Verse 2]
I used to listen to my father pray,
And watch the steam drift slowly away.
I’d bow my head and peek to see
If he was nearly done so we could eat.
Now there are things I want these boys to know
That I was far too young to see back then.
I hear Dad thank the Lord for one more year,
And wish that I could hear that prayer again.

[Chorus: gentle harmonies]
Before we hang the lights this year,
Let’s thank the One who brought us here.
Let the dishes wait, let the room grow still,
There’s a place in us that only praise can fill.
We name the times You brought us through—
There’s a story in each “thank You.”
Let our children hear those stories clear,
Before we hang the lights this year.

[Bridge: piano softens, tender delivery]
We remember when the money was tight,
Counting what we had late into the night.
The times we thought we couldn’t carry on,
You gave us strength enough to face the dawn.

These are the altars of our lives,
The prayers we prayed, the help supplied.
We tell our boys what You have done,
So they know where our help comes from.

[Verse 3: tender, smiles through sadness]
We speak the names of those we miss,
Remember how they laughed and things they did.
An empty chair, a story told,
A little more their children get to hold.
We smile at something someone used to say,
Then wipe a quiet tear away.
Thank You for the years we got to share,
For love we carry past an empty chair.

[Final Chorus: fuller harmonies, still restrained]
Before we hang the lights this year,
Let’s thank the One who brought us here.
For those we miss and those we’re holding near,
For grace that met us in another year.
We name the times You brought us through—
There’s a story in each “thank You.”
May our children tell these stories, too,
And teach their own to turn to You.
Before we hang the lights this year.

[Outro: almost whispered, piano alone]
The boys bow their heads.
I hold Dawn’s hand.
For all You’ve brought us through…
Thank You.

[End]

albums/hold-the-line/.title: Steel and Nail Prints
albums/hold-the-line/.text:
[Intro]
[Lone bugle, soft military snare]

[Verse 1]
The flag snapped high over Pearl Harbor,
My boy pulled my hand down the pier.
He ran to the guns on the Missouri,
Said, "Dad, how'd they ever get these here?"
Nine barrels long as a schoolhouse,
Shells that weighed as much as a car.
He said, "Nothing could ever beat this ship,"
I said, "Son, let me tell you who we are."

[Verse 2]
I knelt beside him on the teakwood,
Pointed where the Arizona lay,
Told him men stood their post when the bombs fell
And gave everything they had that day.
Then I knocked on the side of that gray steel,
Said, "The guns aren't what made her great."

[Chorus]
She was built to take a hit and keep on sailing,
Built to hold her course through smoke and flame,
Not just made to dish it out, son,
But to take it all and fight again.
And God built a man the same way,
Gave him steel to stand his ground,
To stand between his family and the darkness,
Take the hit, and never go down.

[Verse 3]
He said, "Dad, is that why you're so tough?"
I said, "Son, that strength's not my own.
God gave us these shoulders on purpose,
Rugged hands and a will like stone.
You may never go to war, son,
But there's another war around us all.
A man fights for his wife and his children,
And for the souls who are dying lost.
Some days you'll feel like quitting,
Like the waves are pulling you down,
But with His help you won't be sinking,
He's the One who holds you now."

[Chorus]
She was built to take a hit and keep on sailing,
Built to hold her course through smoke and flame,
Not just made to dish it out, son,
But to take it all and fight again.
And God built a man the same way,
Gave him steel to stand his ground,
To stand between his family and the darkness,
Take the hit, and never go down.

[Bridge]
He had more power than any battleship,
Could've called twelve legions down,
But He held His fire on that hill
And took the hits without a sound.
They raised Him on a cross like a target,
And every sin of the world opened fire.
By His stripes, we are healed,
By His scars, we stand.
If you want to know what a real man looks like,
Look at the nail prints in His hands.

[Verse 4]
Thirty years and a few battle scars later,
I'm the one walking down that pier.
My own boy runs ahead to the cannons,
And I can almost feel Dad here.
I knock on the side of that gray steel,
Hear his words come out of me:
"Son, the guns aren't what made her great,
It's the hits she took to keep us free."

[Final Chorus]
She was built to take a hit and keep on sailing,
Built to hold her course through smoke and flame,
Not just made to dish it out, son,
But to take it all and fight again.
And God built a man the same way,
Gave him steel to stand his ground,
To stand between his family and the darkness,
Take the hit, and never go down.

[Outro]
[Bugle returns, soft]
Take the hit…
Like Jesus did.

[End]
